newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended slightly down on a Monday marked by quiet trade ahead of the looming seasonal festivities, dealers said,
With about 350 million rands worth of shares changing hands trade was dull and prices drifted downwards in the absence of any clear direction from other markets.
"There was a Christmas feeling to the market. That is about the only way you could decribe it...it was neither weak nor strong," one dealer said.
The all-share index dipped 4.0 points to 6,536.4 as industrials shed 26.8 points to end at 7,769.0.
Dealers said there had been some basket-trading of shares as few individual stocks sparked off any interest.

The result was a mixed bag of individual performances from the blue-chips as De Beers continued its strong recent gains and put on 300 cents to 133.00 rand. Other favoured stocks were Anglos which added 325 cents to 247.25 rand and SA Breweries which gained 75 cents to 115.75 rand.
Losers on the day were Richemont which shed 50 cents to 65.25 rand and Johnnic which dropped 75 cents to 50.25 rand.
Dealers said the market was likely to carry on drifting until the New Year as the market closes early on Christmas Eve and then has a two day break.
"Everyone is just winding down until the New Year," one dealer said.
The gold index dipped slightly in a market distinguished by a lack of interest in the face of a steady bullion price. The index lost 8.8 points to 1,493.1.

Futures also drifted down in quiet trade as the all-share March contract stood at 6,020/50 from 6,088 and the industrial contract was at 7,590/612 from 7,692. The gold contract steadied at 1,055/63 from 1,060.
